svg.title: WaySignal system design
svg.desc: Citizen and responder SwiftUI apps and the G-one React web workspace call one FastAPI deployment over HTTPS with JWT bearer tokens. The deployment serves REST routers, the built web app, and a Streamable HTTP MCP server mounted at /mcp that only accepts localhost hosts. Nav AI runs inside the same process and calls /mcp over loopback with the caller's own token, so REST and MCP use the same CommunityService, RouteAssessmentService and MapStateService and the same authorization. Route assessment screens up to eight provider candidates against community reports through a HazardPolicy. Data lives in PostgreSQL on Render, or SQLite for the isolated demo. External providers are OSRM, Open-Meteo, Overpass, ArcGIS and an optional OpenAI Responses API. A multi-stage Dockerfile deploys to Render; GitHub Actions builds the iOS app on macOS.

g.text: Implemented architecture at commit e2d58c6 · one FastAPI deployment · REST and MCP share one service layer
Community reports with photo + map pin
Nav AI chat · Speech in / AVSpeech out
Directions from device, pin or base
OSM tiles loaded in the browser
Served from the API's own origin
HTTPS · REST /api/v1 · Authorization: Bearer <JWT HS256, 15 min> · JSON
CORS allow-list · JWT verify (signed_reporter: sub, role ∈ {citizen, worker}, exp) · bounded request bodies (4 MB for Nav AI)
/health · /docs off in production · SPA shell + static assets mounted at / · /mcp mounted behind AuthenticatedMCP
Role checks live in the services, so a
handler cannot forget them — and the MCP
2 "How do I…" → canned app help, no tools
3 Regex intent → plan of ≤ 4 tool calls
4 MCP client dials /mcp with caller's token
6 Optional LLM rewrite; on failure keep
one implementation for REST, MCP, demo
review lifecycle, optimistic versioning, audit log
screen ≤ 8 candidates, exclude, rank; no fake route
hazard zones, expiring shelters, shelter routing
SQLAlchemy 2 · psycopg 3 · create_all + additive column checks
PostgreSQL on Render (production — never falls back)
SQLite fallback in local dev if Postgres is down
called server-side with httpx; keys never reach clients
nearby facilities for the citizen map
optional; store:false; off without a key
Apple MapKit tiles (iOS) and OSM tiles (web) load directly on the client.
Dockerfile: node:24 builds frontend/dist → python:3.12-slim, runs as non-root uid 10001 · render.yaml: Render web service + managed Postgres, JWT_SECRET generated
GitHub Actions (macos-15): signed iOS Simulator build · Local: scripts/run-ios-demo.sh starts the demo API on :8000 and launches the simulator
